evidence.locator: FFFA through FFFF are reserved for vector pointers
evidence.claim: The 6502 takes its NMI, reset and IRQ vectors from $FFFA-$FFFF. This program's thirteen NMI references all depend on that vector table, and its per-frame logic runs from the NMI handler.

evidence.locator: a write to $3456 is the same as a write to $2006
evidence.claim: PPU register ports mirror every 8 bytes across $2000-$3FFF, so the program's $2006/$2007 writes are the canonical addresses rather than the only ones that would work.
OAMDMA at $4014 takes the high byte of a page and copies it into OAM — the mechanism this program uses to update sprites each frame.

evidence.locator: accessible by writing the bottom 3 bits of $4016
evidence.claim: Controller strobe and read run through $4016, which is how this program reads player input.

note: The NES has no boot ROM, so this proof has no restricted input and runs its execute stage in public CI as well as locally — the only machine here whose rendered frame is checked on every push.
evidence_caveat: Tiers are explicit because the NES sources differ in kind. The 6502 vector claim is PRIMARY — MOS's own programming manual for the CPU the 2A03 derives from. The three NES-specific claims are EXTERNAL-FORMAL: the NESdev wiki, community documentation built from hardware analysis rather than a manufacturer manual, held here as page-attributed source extracts. No Nintendo-published hardware manual is in the library; that remains the acquisition that would make these claims primary.
